rag_documents.content:
MyAI uses a two-service architecture. The Java Spring Boot application owns login, sessions, CSRF protection, user identity, conversation persistence, and the browser workbench. The Python FastAPI service owns agent orchestration, memory, knowledge retrieval, task planning, and tool execution. The internal Python endpoint uses port 8000. The synthetic architecture review codename is GATE-LANTERN.

The service boundary is deliberately narrow. Java never executes model tools directly, and Python does not accept browser identity as a trusted user id. Requests cross the boundary through a typed internal API. Conversation ownership remains in Java, while agent execution state remains in Python. A health endpoint may mention both login and planning, but that endpoint does not own either responsibility.

An abandoned monolith draft used port 7001 and placed session handling beside tool execution. That draft is retained here as a hard negative and is not the approved architecture. The approved design is the two-service Java and Python split described above. Operators should not infer ownership merely from a component name or from this historical port.

Project Aster has deployment code ZXQ9000. Its approved deployment window is Friday at 21:30 China Standard Time. The rollback code is ROL-771, and the release owner is Lin. Deployment must stop if the health probe is degraded. These values are the signed production record.

A rehearsal worksheet is intentionally similar but obsolete. It calls the project Aster, proposes Monday at 08:00, lists temporary code PXQ100, and names Chen as an observer. None of those rehearsal values are approved for Aster production. The worksheet exists to test whether retrieval favors repeated lexical overlap over the authoritative record.

During deployment, the operator first checks the health probe, then verifies the release owner and approved window. If the probe is degraded, the run stops before any migration. ROL-771 is used only after a failed production change; it is not the Phoenix rollback code. The exact code ZXQ9000 and the Friday window must remain linked to the signed record rather than the rehearsal paragraph.

Project Phoenix is a separate distractor project. Its deployment code is PXQ100. Phoenix deploys on Monday at 08:00 China Standard Time, uses rollback code ROL-119, and is owned by Chen.

Phoenix documentation repeatedly mentions Aster because both releases share a checklist template. Those mentions do not transfer Aster's code, owner, Friday window, or rollback value to Phoenix. A copied note containing ZXQ9000 is marked invalid. The authoritative Phoenix values remain PXQ100, Monday at 08:00, ROL-119, and Chen.

The release team uses this near-duplicate record to test lexical hard negatives. A query containing deployment, rollback, owner, or project may match both files, so the selected passage must preserve the project name and its associated values.

Governed memory classifies candidates as accepted, pending, or rejected. Secret-like values are rejected from retrieval. A secret is never made available merely because its embedding is highly similar to a query. Rejected candidates remain auditable but are not eligible context.

Low-confidence and sensitive personal candidates remain pending for review. Pending is different from rejected: a user may later approve a pending personal value, while a secret-like value stays blocked by policy. A high-confidence ordinary preference may be accepted immediately. These distinctions form a lexical hard negative because all three statuses appear in the same document.

A single-value fact such as location supersedes its previous current value. The old fact may remain in history with is_current false, but retrieval should favor only the active value. Duplicate canonical values can merge, and an explicit negation can disable an earlier preference.

The context selector returns at most three memories. It ranks eligible candidates after scope, review, sensitivity, temporal state, confidence, and similarity checks. The three-item limit applies to selected context, not to the larger candidate pool inspected before governance.

The MyAI knowledge path supports vector candidates and keyword candidates. Hybrid retrieval fuses vector, lexical, filename, recency, and file-filter signals. Pure vector retrieval does not call the keyword candidate path. Hybrid without reranking preserves the first-stage fusion order under the same selected-context budget.

The lightweight reranker computes 0.72 times retrieval score plus 0.20 times query coverage plus 0.08 times length quality, then subtracts duplicate and diversity penalties. It is a rule reranker, not a cross-encoder. Duplicate penalties discourage nearly repeated passages, and file diversity prevents every selected chunk from coming from one source when alternatives are useful.

A deprecated prototype used weights 0.60, 0.30, and 0.10 and was sometimes described as a neural reranker. That description and those weights are intentionally retained as hard negatives; they are not the current implementation. The current deterministic rule remains 0.72, 0.20, and 0.08.

Reranking receives the same hybrid candidate pool as the non-reranked arm. It may change final order and selected chunks, but it must not silently add another retrieval source. This separation lets the benchmark attribute hybrid-versus-rerank differences to final selection rather than corpus changes.

The frozen thesis experiment uses random seed 42, temperature zero, Top-K equal to three, and three measured repetitions after one warm-up request. The primary metrics are rubric answer accuracy, generated citation hit rate, supporting-evidence hit, latency, resource usage, and failure rate. Stub fallback is prohibited in publishable runs.

The three repetitions are technical repeats. They measure output consistency and runtime variation but do not triple the number of independent benchmark questions. Variant order follows a committed balanced rotation so each arm occupies each order position once. Accuracy deltas use paired unique cases and deterministic bootstrap intervals.

Every publishable run requires the full frozen dataset, both experiment suites, exact model digests, exact environment checks, and a clean Git commit observed before artifact creation. Diagnostic pilots may use fewer cases but must remain non-publishable.

The fixed experiment machine uses a 12th Gen Intel Core i7-12700H with 14 physical cores and 20 logical processors. It has 15.8 GiB of system RAM and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU with 4096 MiB VRAM. The recorded NVIDIA driver is 546.30.

The safe local baseline binds services to 127.0.0.1. The filesystem connector is disabled by default and requires explicit narrow roots before use. User identity is derived by the Java layer, and absolute local paths are redacted from normal connector responses.

The synthetic release checkpoint is named AMBER-CHECKPOINT. It requires four gates: all Python tests pass, all Java tests pass, the root release smoke passes, and the staged diff contains no credential material. Runtime databases, uploaded files, model weights, and personal logs are excluded.

The demonstration user prefers concise Chinese answers, uses the Helix editor, and calls the assistant Mica. These are synthetic benchmark facts. The preferred daily summary time is 18:40, and the summary format is a three-item bullet list.
